subject: phoenix
pitch: A phoenix rising with its wings flung open. Feathers blaze from deep crimson at the body through orange to golden yellow at the tips, a crest of flame-shaped plumes on its head, long trailing tail feathers like ribbons of fire, glowing amber eyes and a golden hooked beak. Embers and sparks drift off its wings.
reasoning:
I need to plan a single TypeScript module representing a phoenix rising, deciding how to position it so its lowest point sits at ground level while wings spread upward in flight.

Letting the long trailing tail feathers dip toward y≈0 while the body sits around 1.4m works well, with the head pitched upward to suggest ascent. I'm structuring it with a chained spine (hips, chest, neck, head) and jointed wings (shoulder, elbow, wrist), building each feather as an extruded leaf shape fanned outward with colors gradating from crimson to yellow by index.

Designing the wing path and feather fan generator...

Still shaping feather layers...

Each feather gets a two-stop gradient colored root-to-tip, with inner feathers crimson fading and outer ones shifting toward orange/gold, keeping paint counts cheap since they're not limited like flat colors. Now I'm laying out the body's spine chain—hips, chest, neck, head—as a tilted sequence of points forming the torso path.

I should instead create an explicit root joint at the hips, then attach the spine chain to it with a defined parent, avoiding ambiguity about implicit roots. For the body shape, I'll sweep the spine chain with a radius profile tapering from wider at the torso to narrower at the neck, keeping the head as a separate joint parented to the spine tip.

The body gets a countershade gradient from deep crimson to orange. For the head, I'm placing a joint at the spine's end with a forward-up direction, building a sphere for the skull, then separate upper and lower beak parts using a curved bezier sweep for the hooked upper beak and a shorter straight sweep for the jaw, with the jaw as a child joint of the head.

Still placing bone-relative features...

For the crest, I'm building a generic feather helper function that takes a base point, direction, up-reference vector, length, width, colors, and bone data, then computes orthonormal axes to orient each feather. I'm using it to create a fan of flame-like plumes sweeping up and back off the head, with their directions varying sideways to spread into a fan shape.

Now I'm shaping the plume outline itself to look like a flame: wide at the base, wavy and narrowing through the middle, ending in a sharp pointed tip, defining a set of width offsets at different lengths along the shape so it curves asymmetrically without self-intersecting.

Deciding to keep smoothing at default/zero for safety since the low-poly facets already read clearly as a flame shape, avoiding any risky corner-cutting that could break the geometry. Moving on to the tail, I'm planning five long trailing ribbon feathers swept along curved paths from the tail base, fanning outward and sweeping back toward the floor with a tapered radius.

Each ribbon will be a sweep using an elliptical cross-section that thins toward the tip, colored with a crimson-to-gold gradient, and rigged to a tail bone chain extending back from the pelvis through several joints. I'm working out how to bind these sweeps to the tail chain properly, likely skinning each ribbon to a specific tail joint so they follow the chain's motion naturally.

Now I'm plotting out seven ribbon paths symmetrically spread across the tail (k ranging -3 to 3), each starting near the hips, curving down and back, with varying lengths and endpoints near ground level so the longest central ribbons trail lowest while outer ones curl higher, giving a flowing, cascading tail effect.

Shaping the ribbons so they're thin when viewed from the side but wide from behind, giving that fluttering look for a bird rising and seen from front or side angles.

I'll skip tail mantle feathers and instead add shorter side ribbons tipped in gold, coloring the ribbons with a layered gradient sweeping from deep crimson through orange into gold along the ribbon's path. For the legs, I'm working out tucked talons versus trailing extended legs, defining hip, knee, and foot points to create a natural sweep.

Each leg becomes a three-point chain named hip, knee, ankle (mirrored left/right), parented to the spine, with a tapered gold sweep. For feet, I'm adding spike-shaped talons at the ankle tip — three pointing forward-down and one back, colored in dark gold.

Now I'm setting up the wing as another chain: shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand points sweeping upward in a V shape, with a crimson tapered sweep, parented to a chest-level spine joint. Next I need the wing's feather layout along that arm path.

Working out feather angle easing and length formulas...

Still working out feather orientation vectors...

I'm estimating feather triangle counts per wing row to stay performant, then planning ember sparks as small low-poly icosahedrons and tetrahedrons scattered around the wings using seeded randomization for gold/orange particle positions that drift downward.

I'm also considering adding scattered chest feathers via small cone extrusions on the body surface, oriented along surface normals for a flame-like spiky look.

Writing feather placement logic...

I'll skip the thigh feathers and neck ruff, keeping the wing arm as a continuous swept chain. Checking overall scene height with wing tips and crest, it fits fine with a neutral rest pose. Now I'm starting to write the actual TypeScript module, setting up imports and the meta object...

Writing scene code...

Building the wing chains symmetrically for left and right sides...

So pelvis, spine1, spine2, neck1, neck2 with neck2 as the tip, giving the head joint a parent of the spine chain's tip. The wings should parent off spine2 (the chest point), and I'm keeping the chain's joint list with the tip included as the last entry.

I'm laying out the spine points from tail base through to the head, sweeping radii from a thick body down to a thin tail with rounded start, then setting up a countershaded color for the body sweep bone since it's mostly covered by feathers anyway. The head joint parents from the spine tip at the final spine point, with a jaw joint hanging off it as a child.

Now I'm shaping the skull as a sphere scaled slightly flattened and elongated, colored a bright red-orange, attached forward of the head joint. For the tail I'm defining a three-point chain extending backward and downward from the pelvis, parented to the root spine joint with a dedicated tail role.

I'm also setting up ribbon shapes across a range of lateral positions, each with a path curving backward and down toward the ground, with the center ribbons reaching all the way to floor level.

Still working out ribbon radius profile...

Adjusting the taper curve exponent...

Still setting up the skeleton joints... now defining leg bones per side with hip, knee, and ankle joints positioned and chained to the spine, planning two leg spans plus a tip segment.

Toes branch from the ankle with spike bones angled forward in a fan plus one back toe, colored golden with dark talon tips. Setting color constants and starting the crest plumes on the head.

For the crest, I'm placing seven feather bases along the head's top with directions swept backward and outward based on position, tapering the lengths so the center plume is tallest and the side ones shorter, then working out the correct normal orientation so each feather lies flat in a plane spanning front-to-back rather than side-to-side.

I'm also sketching two long trailing crest streamers curving from the head's top back and down, defining their path points and radii with a color gradient, and planning a mirrored pair offset slightly to the sides.

For the wing, I'm sweeping an arm shape with tapering radii and a dark red color along a catmull-rom path, then setting up rows of feather loops with varying counts, scale, lift, width, and thickness to build layered feather coverage across the wing.

Still writing feather geometry...

For coverts I'll shift the ramp offsets slightly cooler, and set up a crimson-to-gold color stop sequence so the gradient reads body-red through tip-gold. For the bone structure, I'm mapping each wing feather's length into three joint segments—shoulder, elbow, and wrist—so bending follows natural anatomy based on position along the path.

I'm worried neighboring feathers in the same row could z-fight since they sit on nearly the same plane, so I'll alternate a small lift offset per feather index to separate them safely within the thickness tolerance. For the ember particles, I'll scatter 36 sparks outward from the wings using randomized offsets, and since I'm unsure of the exact rng helper's API, I'll write my own simple LCG generator instead to avoid relying on undocumented behavior.

Each spark becomes a small octahedron particle attached to the root joint with warm colors. For body feathers, I'm scattering hits across the body surface, filtering out ones facing too far downward, then computing each feather's base position and backward-projected direction from the hit normal, picking bone attachments from the hit data with a spine fallback, and coloring them along a crimson-to-gold gradient based on z-position so the chest reads warmer toward the neck.

Now I'm setting counts and spacing for body versus wing feathers, confirming the hit data includes position, normal, and bone references, and sketching out the ribbon and streamer sweep parameters (section, caps, color, bone). I'm also placing the eyes as small amber spheres on the head bone and working out the jaw and lower beak geometry—positioning the jaw joint relative to the head, then building a tapered rod from the jaw to a point along the beak with flat ends and a gold color.

Finishing the upper beak as a bezier sweep curving from the head forward and slightly up, tapering to a point with gold coloring, then returning the completed root structure.
